channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Jobs and BoC caution shape outlook – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that Canada’s June jobs report is expected to show a sharp slowdown in hiring and a pickup in wage growth. He argues the bar for a hawkish shift by the Bank of Canada (BoC) remains high, with benign inflation and USMCA-related risks limiting hike prospects.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Recovers from three-week low; flat above 1.4150 ahead of jobs data
item.description: The USD/CAD pair stages a modest intraday recovery from the 1.4135 area, or a three-week low touched this Friday, and climbs to the top end of its daily range during the early European session.

item.title: Canada Unemployment Rate forecast to remain unchanged in June
item.description: Markets are anticipating a fairly stable report when Statistics Canada releases its Labour Force Survey on Friday. While the Net Change in Employment is predicted to rise by 10K in June, adding to the 87.8K gain in May, the Unemployment Rate is forecast to stay at 6.6%.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy shift talk supports JPY – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes the Japanese Yen is leading G10 gains after Finance Minister Katayama unexpectedly urged households and the GPIF to increase investments in Japanese financial assets.

item.title: Japan’s Kihara says that specifics of monetary policy to be left to BoJ
item.description: Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said during the European trading session on Friday that the specifics of monetary policy to be left to the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Euro remains pinned at one-year lows against the British Pound as Euro Area inflation moderates
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains on the defensive against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, with the EUR/GBP pair unable to take off from one-year lows at the 0.8515 area. Data from Germany and France confirmed that inflationary pressures moderated in June, which added pressure on the common currency.

item.title: WTI rally takes a timeout amid signs of US-Iran war de-escalation
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil futures on NYMEX trade slightly lower to near $71.50 during the European trading session on Friday. The Oil price extends its correction after posting a fresh over two-week high at $75.73 on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar: AI-driven imports reshape trade – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur says AI-related capital-goods imports are structurally widening the US trade deficit. Strong foreign demand currently helps finance the gap, but weaker confidence in the United States (US) AI (Artificial intelligence) investment story could create risks for the Dollar.

item.title: Oil: Brent retraces gains on fragile ceasefire – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Molly Schwartz notes that Brent Oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains constrained despite a nominal ceasefire between the US and Iran. War insurance costs have risen sharply and shipowners are being advised to pause Hormuz voyages.

item.title: Gold sticks to modest losses; eyes $4,100 as Fed hike bets and Iran risks support USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts fresh sellers on Friday, eroding part of the previous day's gains, though it holds above the $4,100 mark heading into the European session.

item.title: British Pound: Upside risk toward resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: According to UOB’s Quek Ser Leang, GBP/USD’s sharp rebound has left scope to test major resistance at 1.3445, though a clear break is seen as unlikely in the near term. Short-term support lies at 1.3390 and 1.3360.

item.title: United States Dollar Index extends losses as US and Iran attempt to resume talks
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) is trading lower for the third consecutive day on Friday.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar extends correction as US-Iran conflict remains under spotlight
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, July 10:

item.title: Euro: Narrow path for sustained strength against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole writes that Middle East tensions have modestly re-tightened EUR/USD short-term swap rate differentials by around 10bp, though the spread remains wider than pre-war levels.

item.title: Indian Rupee rebounds further, ignoring oil price recovery
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends Thursday’s recovery against the US Dollar (USD) in the opening session on Friday.

item.title: Equities: Tech and chips drive relief rally – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists say a strong semiconductor rally and lower oil prices helped lift global equities. The S&P 500 rebounded as investors rotated from defensive sectors into growth and cyclical stocks, while gains in Micron and SK Hynix reinforced confidence in the AI investment cycle.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Gathers strength above 0.5750, but remains below key technical resistance
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades in positive territory around 0.5775 during the early European session on Friday. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) gathers strength to its strongest level in three weeks against the US Dollar (USD) on a hawkish rate hike from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ).

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rises as oil prices correct, US Dollar faces pressure
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 0.4% higher to near $60.22 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal gains as the US Dollar (USD) continues to remain under pressure amid hopes that the restart of the war between the United States (US) and Iran won’t long last.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Inflation uptick with monsoon support – DBS
item.description: DBS economist Radhika Rao expects India’s June CPI inflation to edge up to 4.1% YoY from 3.9%, driven by food normalisation and fuel-cost pass-through.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish Glapinski undercuts support – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reports that the National Bank of Poland kept rates at 3.75% and a neutral stance, but Governor Adam Glapinski’s press conference was markedly dovish.

item.title: Euro consolidates near 1.1450 as German data confirms easing inflationary pressures
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds minor gains against a somewhat softer US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The pair edged up to the mid-range of the 1.1400s, but it has failed to find acceptance above the top of the last two weeks' trading range, in the area of 1.1475, and is set to close the week practically unchanged.

item.title: Japanese Yen rises as Japan urges pension funds to invest in domestic assets
item.description: The USD/JPY pair tumbles to around 161.50 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) after the reports that Japan plans to encourage pension funds to increase their holdings of domestic financial assets.

item.title: Euro: Range trade bias intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights a modest uptick in EUR/USD momentum, with scope to retest 1.1450 but limited prospects for a sustained break higher. Intraday support is seen at 1.1420 and 1.1405.

item.title: Swiss Franc gives back some early gains against US Dollar, US CPI in focus
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) pares some of its early gains against the US Dollar (USD) during the early European trading session on Friday. The USD/CHF pair is 0.26% lower at around 0.8048 even after a slight recovery move.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats from over two-week high, up a little around 0.6950 vs USD
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts buyers for the second straight day and climbs to a two-and-a-half-week top, around the 0.6970 area, during the Asian session on Friday. Spot prices, however, retreat a few pips in the last hour and currently trade around mid-0.6900s, still up 0.10% for the day.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Edges higher above 1.3400, bullish outlook remains intact
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades in positive territory around 1.3430 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The UK government leadership transition and growing expectations of further Bank of England (BoE) interest rate hikes underpin the British Pound (GBP) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Retakes $72.00; 23.6% Fibo./200-day EMA holds the key for bulls
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – edges higher during the Asian session on Friday, stalling the previous day's retracement slide from the vicinity of a three-week high.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Friday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Sits near weekly top around 1.1450 as bulls flirt with 23.6% Fibo.
item.description: The EUR/USD pair attracts some buyers for the third consecutive day and touches a fresh weekly high, around the 1.1460 area, during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens as receding Fed rate hike bets weigh US Dollar
item.description: The USD/CAD pair loses momentum to near 1.4145 during the early European session on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) weakens against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) on receding expectations of a rate increase from the US Federal Reserve (Fed).
